title: Compare Length, Height and Weight
seo_title: Kindergarten Measurement Worksheets: Longer, Shorter, Taller, Heavier, Lighter
standard_text: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten measurement worksheets: compare length (longer, shorter), height (taller), and weight on a pan balance (heavier, lighter), find the longest and shortest, and learn the words. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line things up at one end to compare length. The heavier side of a balance goes down.
key_sub: Length tells how long, height how tall, and weight how heavy.
body_html:
Things we can measure

WordIt tellsCompare with
Lengthhow longlonger, shorter
Heighthow talltaller, shorter
Weighthow heavyheavier, lighter

Compare length: line them up

Put both things at the same starting line. The one that goes further is longer.

Compare height

Compare weight with a balance

The heavier side goes down. If the balance is level, they weigh the same.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Not lining up the endsStart both at the same line
Thinking the high side is heavierThe heavier side goes down
Thinking bigger is always heavierUse a balance to check

faq.q: What do kindergartners learn about measurement?
faq.a: They learn that things have length, height and weight. They compare two things directly and use words like longer, shorter, taller, heavier and lighter.
Not yet. In kindergarten they compare by lining things up side by side. Measuring with units like cubes or inches starts in Grade 1.

faq.q: How does a pan balance show which is heavier?
faq.a: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. When the two sides are level, the things weigh the same.

faq.q: How can I practice at home?
faq.a: Compare spoons, shoes or toys. Ask: Which is longer? How do you know? Hold two things, one in each hand, and guess which is heavier.
